author: Javier Martín
title: Analysis of the news of the presentation of the NVIDIA Isaac GR00T reference humanoid robot
subtitle: The competitive advantage NVIDIA achieved with Cuda is on its way to being repeated with Isaac
body_markdown:
![Image](https://substack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com/public/images/3680cda4-ad6b-474c-aba8-38b313f044d9_1600x900.jpeg)

**NVIDIA** has just taken an important step toward solving one of the big current problems of humanoid robotics: benchmarks for the quality of robot performance. Something that was immediate with the appearance of LLMs, where very strong people in AI, such as François Chollet, devoted themselves to devising ways of evaluating the quality of artificial intelligence models.

Now in robotics we have something similar, because the [Isaac GR00T Reference Humanoid Robot for Academic Research](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-open-humanoid-robot-reference-design?ncid=so-twit-539319-vt48) is not just the way NVIDIA wants to repeat in Physical AI the GPU+CUDA play that has also worked for it in Generative AI, but is the missing piece for knowing whether the developments of VLAs and WAMs that many labs are carrying out are on the path to achieving general-purpose robots.

In this way, what NVIDIA is doing is deploying all its technical and media power to drive humanoid robots, which will result in an increasingly strong **Physical AI development ecosystem** and the gradual resolution of problems regarding robots' real capabilities to perform everyday tasks in the real world.

And this is where we have to think about which robotics labs may be the first to turn to this robot to advance their research, and although the news mentions Ai2, ETH Zurich, the Stanford Robotics Center and UC San Diego's Advanced Robotics and Controls Lab, the truth is that there are currently many very well-funded startups that can benefit greatly from having a standardized development platform like this one. In this list we could include Skild AI, Generalist, Physical Intelligence, Field AI, Genesis, OpenMind, … But not only that: the robotics labs of many large tech companies that until now were testing their AI models with robotic arms, such as Meta, Apple, OpenAI, Alibaba, Google Deepmind, … now also have a robot they can buy in large quantities to advance their research.

And this matter of buying the robot in large quantities is where the key lies regarding the participation of **Unitree** and **Sharpa Wave**, because with them the circle closes to be able to offer a complete robot.

For Unitree this is excellent news, since before its IPO it receives the support of NVIDIA, which is saying that at the moment it is the manufacturer most capable of producing robots in large volumes. On the other hand, for Sharpa Wave it is a big boost, because it puts this company on the map and positions it as the spearhead in dexterity with its 22-degree-of-freedom hand.

And now let's dwell a little on the software side NVIDIA provides in this initiative, because GPUs for robots are fairly well understood given the similarity with what happened in training and inference of AI models, but for robotics what the company is doing is presenting an enormous number of options worth knowing about. They are the following tools:

- **NVIDIA Isaac Teleop** allows a person to operate the robot and record good demonstrations of how a task is done. Those examples are then used to train the robot.
- **NVIDIA Isaac GR00T** is the set of AI models that helps the humanoid understand instructions, learn tasks and perform different behaviours.
- **NVIDIA Isaac Sim** and Isaac Lab make it possible to test the robot in simulation before taking it into the real world. That is, to train it, check for failures and evaluate whether a task works without risking the physical robot.
- NVIDIA Isaac's accelerated **ROS** helps the real robot perform the actions for which it has been trained in simulation or in the lab through teleoperation.

Therefore, the presentation of the NVIDIA Isaac GR00T reference robot does not yet signal the arrival of the generalist humanoid robot; rather, it positions itself at an earlier step, which is also very important: building a common platform for teaching, simulating, evaluating and deploying physical AI in humanoid robots. Something the company already did at the time when it created the whole software ecosystem through Cuda, which has given it an enormous competitive advantage that for now no competitor is managing to replicate.

items.headline: 🚗 BMW will deploy humanoids in production in Germany for the first time, starting with a pilot in Leipzig with Hexagon Robotics and its AEON robot.
items.body_markdown: 🚗 [BMW](https://www.press.bmwgroup.com/global/article/detail/T0455864EN/bmw-group-to-deploy-humanoid-robots-in-production-in-germany-for-the-first-time?language=en) will deploy humanoids in production in **Germany** for the first time, starting with a pilot in Leipzig with Hexagon Robotics and its AEON robot. BMW also shares results from the Figure 02 pilot in Spartanburg: more than 30,000 BMW X3s assisted, 90,000 components moved and some 1,250 hours of operation, a very strong sign that humanoids are starting to enter real factories.

items.headline: 🏥 NVIDIA partners with Foxconn and Taiwanese medical centres to bring agentic AI and physical AI to the healthcare system.
items.body_markdown: 🏥 [NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-foxconn-and-taiwan-medical-centers-bring-agentic-and-physical-ai-to-healthy-taiwan) partners with **Foxconn** and Taiwanese medical centres to bring agentic AI and physical AI to the healthcare system. Foxconn is deploying CoDoctor AI, specialized clinical agents and collaborative robots such as Nurabot, with NVIDIA NemoClaw, Isaac for Healthcare and Omniverse as the basis for moving from pilots to real operations in hospitals.

items.headline: 🤖 OpenAI Robotics is hiring hardware, operations, systems and machine learning profiles to build robots useful to society.
items.body_markdown: 🤖 [OpenAI Robotics](https://x.com/sama/status/2061117302528188712?s=46) is hiring hardware, operations, systems and machine learning profiles to build robots useful to society. **Sam Altman** explains that the world simulation programme led by Aditya Ramesh has evolved into OpenAI Robotics, with a clear thesis: combining ML research and hardware co-design to bring AI into the physical world.

items.headline: 📱 COBALT presents a cloud teleoperation system for robot learning using smartphones.
items.body_markdown: 📱 [COBALT](https://cobalt-teleop.github.io/) presents a cloud teleoperation system for **robot learning** using smartphones. The idea is to turn a phone into a control interface for collecting data in simulation and in real environments, including bimanual tasks, which points to a cheaper and more scalable way to generate human demonstrations without expensive teleoperation hardware.

items.headline: 🇯🇵 Atom is a new Japanese humanoid robot company that has announced a seed round of 3 billion yen.
items.body_markdown: 🇯🇵 [Atom](https://x.com/aoshun7/status/2059439540084113918?s=46) is a new Japanese humanoid robot company that has announced a seed round of 3 billion yen. Its founder, Shunsuke Aoki, points to three key challenges: developing **physical AI** models, designing data collection lines and building the supply chain needed to manufacture humanoids.

items.headline: 🧢 Human Archive is using service workers in India to collect egocentric data of everyday tasks.
items.body_markdown: 🧢 [Human Archive](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/26/human-archive-taps-into-indias-services-startups-to-collect-data-for-physical-ai/) is using service workers in India to **collect egocentric data** of everyday tasks. The startup already has more than 1,000 active devices, has raised 8.2 million dollars and is betting on combining video, depth, tactile gloves, motion capture and wrist cameras to train robots with real human work data.

items.headline: 🏭 Eden Robotics presents autonomous robots for industry under a Robots-as-a-Service model.
items.body_markdown: 🏭 [Eden Robotics](https://edenrobotics.ai/) presents autonomous robots for industry under a **Robots-as-a-Service** model. Its proposal combines plug-and-play deployment, 24/7 operations, zero installation cost and prices from 10 dollars an hour, reinforcing an important trend: selling automation as an operational service, not as a hardware purchase.

items.headline: 🌌 NVIDIA AI presents Cosmos 3, its new frontier model for physical AI.
items.body_markdown: 🌌 [NVIDIA AI](https://x.com/NVIDIAAI/status/2061308434629132553) presents **Cosmos 3**, its new frontier model for physical AI. NVIDIA describes it as an open omnimodel with native visual reasoning, world generation and action generation, available in 32B Super and 8B Nano variants, a key piece for connecting perception, simulation and robotic action.

items.headline: 📊 Mecka announces 60 million dollars in funding to become the data and deployment layer of physical AI.
items.body_markdown: 📊 [Mecka](https://x.com/joshavata/status/2061481322737267152) announces 60 million dollars in funding to become the **data and deployment layer of physical AI**. The company wants to scale its data infrastructure, enter new verticals and deploy robots in the real world, attacking precisely one of the sector's big bottlenecks: turning physical data into useful robotic systems.

items.headline: 🔬 Luma launches the Open Physical AI Lab to research generalization in robotics.
items.body_markdown: 🔬 [Luma](https://x.com/gravicle/status/2061476460217737294) launches the **Open Physical AI Lab** to research generalization in robotics. Its thesis is that physical AI is experiencing a crisis of data and generalization: robots still learn specific tasks in specific environments, and the solution cannot just be scaling teleoperation, but building world models and open tools so that more teams can create physical systems.

items.headline: 🎥 Runway joins as a founding member of the Cosmos Coalition, a global initiative with NVIDIA and other labs to build and open frontier world models for physical AI.
items.body_markdown: 🎥 [Runway](https://x.com/runwayml/status/2061315089869721682) joins as a founding member of the **Cosmos Coalition**, a global initiative with NVIDIA and other labs to build and open frontier world models for physical AI. The news connects generative video labs with robotics: simulating the world stops being just visual content and starts becoming infrastructure for training physical agents.

items.headline: 🧹 Shift launches a free home cleaning service in New York in exchange for recording data of the task.
items.body_markdown: 🧹 [Shift](https://x.com/joinshiftx/status/2060044783519735987?s=46) launches a free **home cleaning** service in New York in exchange for recording data of the task. A human operator goes to the home with a device, cleans, and the recording is anonymized to feed robotics datasets, a model that turns everyday services into a data production line for household robots.

items.headline: 🦾 Ilir Aliu summarizes a low-cost route for starting to train real robots at home for less than 300 dollars.
items.body_markdown: 🦾 [Ilir Aliu](https://x.com/iliraliu_/status/2059334512123711821?s=46) summarizes a low-cost route for starting to train real robots at home for less than 300 dollars. The combination of **MuJoCo**, an SO-101 arm, LeRobot, ACT policies, a webcam and multimodal models shows that robot learning is entering a much more accessible phase for makers, students and independent researchers.
